extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH grant applications (PHS 398 / R21) / principal investigators and institutional grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and assemble components of a PHS 398-format NIH research application (R21 example), including Specific Aims, Research Strategy (Significance, Innovation, Approach), modular budget and required attachments. Focus is on presenting experimental design, controls, validation, personnel allocation, and requisite compliance sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Embryonic Stem Cells
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposed project involve human embryonic stem cells? If the proposed project involves human embryonic stem cells, list below the registration number of the specific cell line(s) from the following list: http://stemcells.nih.gov/research/registry/. Or, if a specific stem cell line cannot be referenced at this time, check the box indicating that one from the registry will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide registry numbers for specific cell line(s) if known. If unknown, explicitly check the box that a registry-listed line will be used. Failure to provide required registry information or checkbox may render the application non-compliant with NIH HESC policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Modular Budget completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete modular budget sections for each budget period: Start Date, End Date, Budget Period, Direct Cost less Consortium F&AA, Direct Costs, Indirect Costs, Consortium F&A, Total Direct Costs, Indirect Cost Type, Indirect Cost Rate (%), Indirect Cost Base ($), Funds Requested ($), Cognizant Agency (Agency Name, POC Name and Phone Number), Indirect Cost Rate Agreement Date, Total Indirect Costs, and C. Total Direct and Indirect Costs (A + B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate dollar amounts for Funds Requested for each period and cumulative totals. Fill in indirect cost type/rate and cognizant agency/contact and agreement date. If consortium F&A applies, show separate accounting. Ensure modular budget format matches NIH modular budget instructions (rounding to modules where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification (Personnel, Consortium, Narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Budget Justification attachments: Personnel Justification, Consortium Justification, Additional Narrative Justification. For personnel, list name/title, role, calendar months (effort), and specific responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe responsibilities for each named person (e.g., PI responsible for overall intellectual direction, supervision, protocol/data review, training of personnel). For trainees/staff include months and duties (e.g., Post-doc primary responsibility for GPS screens). Attach supporting justification documents and budgets for consortium organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan Attachments (required sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach applicable sections of the Research Plan in the specified order: Type of Application; Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Protection of Human Subjects; Inclusion of Women and Minorities; Targeted/Planned Enrollment Table; Inclusion of Children; Vertebrate Animals; Consortium/Contractual Arrangements; Letters of Support; Resource Sharing Plan(s); Appendix. Include Introduction to Application for resubmission or revision when applicable and Human Subjects Sections where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each required attachment is present and labeled. For resubmissions/renewals include the Introduction and Progress Report Publication List as applicable. Missing required attachments will affect compliance and may impact review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: State clear, concise Specific Aims that summarize the overall goal and list discrete, numbered aims (e.g., Specific Aim 1: Identify and characterize host cell proteins stabilized or destabilized by L. pneumophila effectors; Specific Aim 2: Determine the Dot/Icm-translocated substrates responsible for alterations in host protein stability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific Aims should articulate what will be accomplished and why it matters. Aims must be testable and aligned to Significance and Approach. Keep aims succinct and numbered; link downstream experiments and expected impact (e.g., potential to identify host targets for therapeutics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the problem is important and how the proposed work will advance knowledge or clinical practice (e.g., studying bacterial manipulation of host protein stability at a global scale fills a gap left by transcriptional studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the knowledge gap, how addressing it will move the field forward, and potential broader impacts (e.g., identification of host proteins required for pathogen replication enabling host-based therapeutics). Make relevance compelling to a broad audience in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the project challenges current paradigms or introduces novel concepts, methods, or tools (e.g., adapting the Global Protein Stability (GPS) system to examine pathogen-mediated changes in host protein stability is an innovative, scalable approach).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize novelty relative to existing methods (why prior approaches are limited) and how the proposed adaptation or new technique expands capability (e.g., moving from microarray-based counting to deep sequencing to increase resolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (experimental design, feasibility, and specific methods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed experimental plan describing key experiments, comparisons, sample handling, measurements and expected outcomes (e.g., infect pooled ORFeome-expressing HEK293T libraries with wild-type and ΔdotA L. pneumophila, sort cells by EGFP:DsRed ratios into 7 bins, PCR-amplify ORFs from bins, hybridize to custom arrays, compute PSI and ΔPSI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include rationale for experimental choices, preliminary data demonstrating feasibility, explicit description of methods (infection conditions, sorting strategy, number of cells per bin), anticipated results and interpretation, and contingency plans for limitations or unexpected results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls and hybridization / assay quality controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and describe appropriate internal and cross-array controls: show that DsRed and EGFP expressed alone are not altered by infection; include array spike-in controls labeled at predetermined ratios; use multiple probes per ORF to assess consistency; compare Cy5 pre-sort signals across arrays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate assay specificity and reproducibility by reporting control results. Explain how controls address potential technical noise from microarrays and justify steps taken to minimize artifactual PSI changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitation, metrics and data analysis robustness
rubrics_metrics.description: Define quantitative metrics and analysis pipelines (e.g., compute Protein Stability Index (PSI) per ORF from 1–7 indicating stability, compute ΔPSI by subtracting wild-type from ΔdotA PSI to measure effector impact; microarray Cy3:Cy5 ratio usage; theoretical range and interpretation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how PSI is calculated and interpreted, statistical considerations, handling of probe-level variability, thresholds for calling hits, and planned improvements (e.g., transition to deep sequencing-based bin quantitation to increase resolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hit validation and orthogonal confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate screening ‘hits’ using small-scale, orthogonal assays: pick candidate ORFs, clone into GPS vector individually, package retrovirus, transduce cells, infect with wild-type and mutant strains, perform flow cytometry to measure EGFP:DsRed shifts and confirm by immunoblotting under endogenous expression when antibodies available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen hits are hypotheses requiring confirmation. Validation should include re-testing single ORFs, biochemical assays (immunoblots), and functional tests (does reversing stability affect bacterial intracellular growth). Describe criteria for advancing validated hits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library coverage and scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the ORFeome/library resources and plan for scaling coverage (e.g., use ORFeome v3.1 library of ~12,000 ORFs with plan to use v5.1 (17,000 ORFs) and ultimately aim for near-complete coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State how library composition affects discovery breadth, plans for future library upgrades, and how increased coverage and sequencing-based quantitation will enable deeper network and pathway analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel qualifications, roles and effort allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Document key personnel with titles, calendar months/effort, and explicit responsibilities (e.g., PI: overall intellectual direction and supervision; Post-doc: primary responsibility for GPS screens and effector identification; Research Assistant: cell culture and molecular biology support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide justification that named personnel have appropriate expertise for assigned tasks and that effort allocation is sufficient to complete proposed work. Make sure months of effort are consistent between personnel justification and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects, inclusions, vertebrate animals and select agent compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Include applicable protection and compliance sections: Protection of Human Subjects, Inclusion of Women and Minorities, Targeted/Planned Enrollment Table, Inclusion of Children, Vertebrate Animals, Select Agent Research, and other Human Subjects Sections as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed sections addressing protections, enrollment plans, rationale for inclusion/exclusion, and biosafety/agent handling plans. Attach required forms and documentation; failure to address compliance areas can affect review and funding.
